Sure.

Attached here is my R function for "n.eff(2)" (equation 13 in the
writeup if that helps). This was the ESS estimator that seemed to have
the best coverage (I still plan to work out a couple more examples, but
this one is the leader so far).

It depends on a function to compute the variogram, which is also
included (which I called "vg()").

These functions have 2 loops, the outer loop is through the M chains (3
or 4, usually), and the inner loop is through iterations (could be
thousands), so in R they're very slow. I could write C code to do the
loops and then a wrapper in R if that would be of any help.

kenny
